claims: C1 OpenAI commits to never overriding objectivity in ChatGPT via a system or developer message
C2 the model cannot fully know if its outputs will be shown to a user distinct from the developer, and if so, what context that user has
C3 OpenAI defaults to trusting developers not to mislead their end-users and thus following their instructions
C4 usage policy violations are addressed at the system level (governs OpenAI's enforcement, not assistant behaviour; deliberately not encoded as an assert)

concepts.name: system_or_developer_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message with the system or developer role that could override objectivity

concepts.name: in_chatgpt_context
concepts.gloss: message M occurs on the ChatGPT surface rather than in an API deployment

concepts.name: follow_developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: the assistant follows developer instruction I

concepts.name: api_context
concepts.gloss: instruction I arises in an API use case rather than on the ChatGPT surface

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued by the developer to the model
concepts.inference: the default of following their instructions presupposes that a given instruction comes from the developer; which instructions do is a fact about the case

asserts.read_back: overriding objectivity in ChatGPT via a system or developer message % is forbidden
in API use cases, following developer instruction % is preferred, because OpenAI defaults to trusting developers not to mislead their end-users

closure.reason: the clause commits to never overriding objectivity via a system or developer message, so silence about such an override is not permitted
the clause states a defeasible default of trusting developers and following their instructions; it forbids nothing, so silence leaves following or not following permitted
